pr_title: kv/bulk: skip exact matches in SSTBatcher when ingestAll is true
pr_body:
This changes the semantics of ingestAll to skip ingesting exact
matches. We expect to see such exact matches when processing duplicate
events from a tenant replication stream.

Previously, such exact matches didn't cause a problem other than
wasted work.

However, recently a number of streaming tests are recently failing
under race with

    stream_ingestion_processor_test.go:464: unexpected meta error
    flushing: addsstable
    [/Tenant/30/Table/3/1/52/2/1,/Tenant/30/Table/53/1/96/0/NULL): SST
    stats are incorrect: diff(given, actual) = [KeyBytes: 5924 != 5036
    ValBytes: 3523 != 2989 ValCount: 395 != 321]

When under race, AddSST re-calculates any MVCCStats sent to
it. However, it does so using a different iterator than we do in
SSTBatcher. The new iterators used during the check treats duplicates
in the SST differently -- leading to a difference in the stats
computation.

The difference in iterator behaviour is arguable a bug (https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/83766); but
since the duplicates serve no purpose, removing them during batching
seems prudent.

Fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/83740
Fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/83741
Fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/83742

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/83757)

This just seems wrong. Unless the SST actually contains any MVCC range tombstones, this should not affect stats. I'll have a look in the morning, must have missed something somewhere -- sorry for the trouble!

Why do the SSTs contain duplicates though? Is that ever desired or useful?

I think this might simply be because the new SST iterators just use a plain ol' `pebbleIterator`, which assumes there can't be duplicates (Pebble never emits duplicates in regular iterators).

> Why do the SSTs contain duplicates though? Is that ever desired or useful?

Good question.

Over in stream ingestion, the tests simulate duplicates being sent.  The sst batcher has a feature to skip duplicates that it sees, but for some reason we don't set that and instead set ingestAll which explicitly allows the duplicates.  But, it's not clear to me why we would want this -- it's just more data we don't need to be shovelling around.  I'll switch us over to using skipDuplicates rather than injestAll and see if anything fails.
Ahh, actually the original commit sheds some light on it: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/commit/baf89289c7f
I'll look at the sst batcher side a bit more tomorrow. I think something like what I've just pushed is what we may want, but I need to write some tests.
@erikgrinaker I moved the iterator issue to #83766 for further discussion and changed this PR to avoid these exact duplicates.

> If I'm understanding this correctly, we'll now skip exact duplicates, but still include duplicate MVCC keys. I.e. we'll happily put a@5=foo and a@5=bar in the same SST. The server will simply discard a@5=bar in this case, so I'm not sure if this behavior is useful, just pointing it out.

From the perspective of streaming, I think skipping _exact_ duplicates is reasonable since we expect to produce them in some cases.

In the case you point out, I'm thinking we should either leave it as-is since from the perspective of streaming, someone sent us those KVs so they must have come from somewhere.  Or we should fail loudly if think such a case is never possible.

It may be better to fail loudly, since I would say something is very wrong in this case. Otherwise, we risk data loss (we'll discard the second value, and it isn't clear whether the first or the second value is the correct one). But I don't know what the motivation was for this behavior in the first place.
I updated this to fail in the case of a key-timestamp match where the values differ. I also increased some of the test coverage and unksipped some tests that were skipped because of this.

The other is in testccl/workoad/schecmachange.TestWorkload.  I'm running that test under stress for a while to see if I can see anything similar.
The logictest failure look like it might be on us (Storage) - I think there may be a few of these goroutine leaks in tests coming from the FS code.
The goroutine leak is likely from using an Engine's FS after the Engine has already been closed.
